summary: Enterprise customer: p95 latency spikes during long-prompt batch windows (mixed workload contention); request mitigation guidance
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports repeatable p95 tail spikes on interactive chat endpoints when long-context summarization jobs are running in the same Dedicated cluster.
- Symptom pattern matches known mixed-workload contention: long prefill-heavy requests create batching/queueing windows that block short/interactive traffic.

Customer impact
- Interactive chat route intermittently breaches internal p95 target (customer states: from ~450–650ms baseline to 2.5–4.0s for ~10–20 minute windows).
- Downstream timeouts observed in customer app at ~5s timeout threshold.
- Customer escalation request: “We need a mitigation we can safely enable without changing our API integration.”

Environment
- Dedicated: hf-ded-03 (us-east)
- Routes:
  - /v1/chat/completions (streaming, interactive)
  - /v1/completions (non-streaming, long-context summarization)
- Models: rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct primary; rw-mistral-large-2 fallback enabled

What changed / when it started
- Customer indicates issue became visible after they onboarded a nightly summarization workload (long prompts, 16k–64k context) to the same cluster ~2 weeks ago.
- No Redwood release change correlated in the customer’s reported start window (needs confirmation via cluster release audit).

Initial hypothesis
- Mixed workload scheduling/queueing effects: long prefill requests occupying prefill slots / head-of-line blocking for short requests.
- Potential priority inversion under overload if admission control is shared.

Data requested from customer
- Example request IDs / timestamps spanning a spike window
- Typical prompt length and max_tokens for summarization workload
- Confirmation of concurrency settings on both routes

Redwood notes
- We have an in-flight prototype scheduler (short/long prompt-aware) behind a feature flag in runtime-1.19 that specifically targets this class of regression. Proposed customer-safe next step: enable in a test slice / staging first, then a limited canary in prod if metrics are favorable.

Attachments / links (internal)
- Dashboards: Dedicated cluster overview (latency + queue depth): rwd://dashboards/dedicated/hf-ded-03
- Traces: sampled trace search query: rwd://traces?cluster=hf-ded-03&service=runtime-scheduler
- Related internal effort: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype (ENG-4821 umbrella)
comments:
2025-01-14 09:12 PT — Aisha Bello (Reporter)
Created ticket from #support escalation. Customer (HelioFin Analytics) reports p95 spikes on interactive route when long-context summarization batch kicks off. Tagged SRE + runtime scheduler SMEs.

Customer quote excerpt:
“Chat latency jumps to multiple seconds whenever our summarization pipeline runs. We can reproduce it daily. We need stability on p95.”

2025-01-14 10:03 PT — Rafael Mendes (Assignee)
Acknowledged. Assigning to myself for triage; pulling metrics now.

Initial checks
- Cluster hf-ded-03 appears at ~70–85% GPU util during spike windows.
- p95 for /v1/chat/completions aligns with customer report (peaks 2.8–3.6s).
- Correlated rise in runtime queue depth + increased prefill time variance.

Next
- Request IDs + timestamps from customer for a specific window to correlate with traces.
- Loop in runtime scheduler team (Sofia / Omar) for mixed-workload analysis.

2025-01-14 10:26 PT — Omar El-Sayed (Runtime perf + observability)
Looked at the time-series: you can see periodic ‘prefill-dominant’ waves. Short requests are waiting behind long-prefill batches (classic HOL blocking).

I recommend we capture:
- scheduler.queue_depth{class=short|long}
- scheduler.wait_ms p95 by class
- prefill_ms vs decode_ms split

If those aren’t present on this cluster build, we should at least add temporary sampled logs. This maps closely to the mixed-workload scheduler prototype we’re validating.

2025-01-14 11:02 PT — Sofia Ivanova (EM Scheduling)
This matches the failure mode we designed the prototype for.

Mitigation options (in increasing confidence):
1) Operational: isolate summarization workload to separate route/model pool (if customer willing). Fastest but may require config change.
2) Enable mixed-workload scheduler feature flag on a test environment and evaluate.

Flag name (runtime-1.19+): runtime.scheduler.mixed_workload.enable=true
Key guardrails:
- long-queue fairness window enabled by default
- separate admission thresholds by class recommended under overload

We should NOT flip this in prod without a canary + rollback plan. Suggest: 10% traffic slice for hf-ded-03 if they have a staging shard; otherwise do a 1-hour controlled window during their batch with tight monitoring.

2025-01-14 12:18 PT — Rafael Mendes (Assignee)
Customer update sent (via CSM): We can reproduce internal correlation and are proposing two mitigation paths:
- Near-term: partial workload isolation (separate route/model pool) to prevent contention.
- Medium-term: test enabling a new scheduler policy behind a flag that prioritizes short/interactive requests while ensuring long prompts don’t starve.

Asked customer for:
- a) 5–10 request IDs from a spike window
- b) their summarization schedule + concurrency
- c) whether a staging / canary window is acceptable this week

2025-01-15 08:41 PT — Rafael Mendes (Assignee)
Customer provided timestamps (Jan 14 19:05–19:25 UTC) and request IDs (stored in internal notes, not pasted here).

Trace correlation
- Long summarization requests show prefill times 8–15s with large variance.
- During those prefills, short interactive requests show queue wait inflation (wait_ms p95 > 2s) while service time is relatively stable.

Interpretation
- Tail spike is dominated by queueing delay, not decode throughput.

Proposed next step
- Stand up a test slice with runtime-1.19 build and enable mixed-workload scheduler flag.
- Run the customer’s batch pattern (or replay a trace-like load) while monitoring queue/wait metrics + p95 on chat.

I’m coordinating with release + runtime; will propose a canary plan once we confirm build availability on hf-ded-03.

2025-01-15 09:30 PT — Connor O'Brien (Release train)
hf-ded-03 is currently on runtime-1.18.7. runtime-1.19.0 is available for dedicated canary rings but not rolled to all clusters.

We can do one of:
- Upgrade a staging shard / canary ring to 1.19.0 and test the flag.
- If no staging exists, we can temporarily canary a subset of pods in hf-ded-03 (requires customer approval + SRE coverage).

Rollback is straightforward (revert pod set) as long as we keep config default-off and do not change API surface.

2025-01-15 11:14 PT — Aisha Bello (SRE)
If we proceed with canary:
Monitoring must include (minimum):
- chat p95/p99 + error rate
- queue depth by class (if available)
- long-queue starvation signal / max wait
- overall throughput + GPU util

Rollback triggers (suggested):
- chat p95 regresses >15% from baseline for 10+ min
- 5xx increases >0.2% absolute
- long-queue max wait exceeds configured bound or sustained backlog growth

Please ensure on-call coverage during customer’s batch window.

2025-01-16 07:22 PT — Rafael Mendes (Assignee)
Internal alignment: Sofia + Omar agree this is the best candidate customer for validating the mixed-workload scheduler (it’s exactly long summarization + interactive chat).

Customer-facing proposal drafted:
- Create hf-ded-03-canary (small pod subset) on runtime-1.19.
- Enable runtime.scheduler.mixed_workload.enable=true in canary only.
- Run during their normal summarization window.
- Compare canary vs baseline on chat p95 + timeouts; confirm no long job starvation.

Awaiting customer approval to proceed with the canary window.

2025-01-17 10:05 PT — Rafael Mendes (Assignee)
Customer approved a controlled test in a non-production environment first.

Action items
- SRE: provision a test shard (hf-ded-03-stg) or a traffic shadow setup if stg shard isn’t available.
- Runtime: confirm metrics availability (queue class instrumentation) on the 1.19 build we’ll use.
- Support/CS: schedule test run aligned with their summarization load (or provide replay harness instructions).

Status remains In Progress pending completion of test + results readout.
resolution: Pending. Proposed mitigation is to evaluate mixed-workload scheduler prototype (feature-flagged) in a test environment, then canary in prod if successful. Immediate workaround option is workload isolation (separate capacity pool/route) to prevent long-prefill requests from impacting interactive traffic.
